head: working-tree
subject: MQTT router match and shared selection join the harnessz baseline gate
change: The router benchmark was a fixed-loop executable with destructive subscription churn and no baseline support. A new examples/bench_mqtt_router_match.zig keeps the same 4,098-filter trie and 64-member shared-group setup but samples only the read-only scenarios with harnessz: router-match, the linear-scan comparison, and the round-robin, sticky, random and rendezvous shared selections. The benchmark is registered in build.zig as bench-mqtt-router-match and in the bench-record/bench-gate sets with benchmarks/baselines/mqtt-router.json. Destructive churn scenarios remain in the original bench-mqtt-router executable.

benchmark.command: zig build bench-record -Doptimize=ReleaseFast (records all sampler-backed baselines)

direct_gate.note: all six entries compared within noise immediately after recording; router-match 1.030x and rendezvous 1.093x were faster than the recorded medians

full_gate.note: the serialized gate ran all eight sampler-backed benchmarks, including the six router entries

notes: The linear scenario uses 100 iterations per callback because one 4,098-filter scan is about 103 us; ten samples still give a stable median. The shared routers are recreated per strategy so the cursor and random state start from the same point as the fixed-loop benchmark. The benchmark records ns per callback; dividing by the iteration count gives 74 ns for router-match, 103.3 us for the linear scan, 130-138 ns for round-robin/sticky/random, and 1.04 us for rendezvous. Baseline files under benchmarks/baselines/ are local generated artifacts. The gate remains host-load sensitive and should be judged on a quiet host; this run used --warn-only while other sessions were active.
